title: Māori traditions
subtitle: Atua, ancestors and pūrākau
about: The atua, ancestors, voyagers, creatures and sky lore of Māori pūrākau, from the separation of Ranginui and Papatūānuku to the feats of Māui and the rising of Matariki. Cards draw mainly on Te Ara, the Encyclopedia of New Zealand, with Te Aka Māori Dictionary for spellings; traditions differ between iwi, and notes say where widely told versions vary.

cards.prompt: Sky father, pushed up and away from the earth
cards.note: Dew is said to be his tears, falling on Papatūānuku as he mourns their separation; the heavens were thought to have 10 or 12 layers.

cards.prompt: Earth mother, from whom all life is born
cards.note: Whenua means both land and placenta, and a newborn's whenua is traditionally buried in a significant place, binding the child to the land.

cards.prompt: Atua of forests and birds, who separated his parents
cards.note: In a Te Arawa account he lay on his back and pushed with arms and legs; other tellings have him standing on his head.

cards.prompt: Atua of the sea and the creatures in it
cards.note: In most tellings he is a son of Ranginui and Papatūānuku; a Ngāti Raukawa account instead makes him Papatūānuku's husband.

cards.prompt: Atua of wind and storms, who opposed the separation
cards.note: He rose to live with his father, then attacked his brothers in revenge, snapping Tāne's trees and raising Tangaroa's waves as tall as mountains.

cards.prompt: Atua of war and of humankind
cards.note: Alone among the brothers he stood firm against Tāwhirimātea's storms; the New Zealand Army is known in Māori as Ngāti Tūmatauenga.

cards.prompt: Atua of kūmara, cultivated food and peace
cards.note: Often simply Rongo. When Tāwhirimātea attacked, he hid inside Papatūānuku, which is said to be why kūmara grow underground.

cards.prompt: Atua of fern root and uncultivated food
cards.note: Also called Haumia or Haumia-tikitiki. He hid in the earth from Tāwhirimātea's storms, which is why aruhe, edible fern root, burrows underground.

cards.prompt: Atua of earthquakes and volcanoes
cards.note: Still at his mother's breast when she was turned face down, he was given fire for warmth; earthquakes are his footsteps below.

cards.prompt: Atua of darkness, evil and death
cards.note: In Wairarapa traditions he fought Tāne for the three baskets of knowledge, sending insects, birds and bats to attack him, and lost.

cards.prompt: Atua of death, who receives the dead in the underworld
cards.note: Once Hine-tītama, daughter of Tāne and Hine-ahu-one, she fled to te pō on learning that her husband Tāne was also her father.

cards.prompt: Atua of fire, from whom Māui won flame
cards.note: Te Ara calls her Māui's grandmother. In a Mātaatua tradition she married the comet Auahi-tūroa and bore five children, the five fingers.

cards.prompt: First woman, shaped by Tāne from earth at Kurawaka
cards.note: Her name means earth-formed woman. Tāne gave her both te ira atua and te ira tangata, so people share divine and human natures.

cards.prompt: Atua of childbirth, weaving and women's arts
cards.note: Also written Hineteiwaiwa. In many tellings she is the wife of Tinirau; Te Ara also links her with the moon and fertility.

cards.prompt: Mother who cast newborn Māui into the sea in her topknot
cards.note: Hence his full name, Māui-tikitiki-a-Taranga. He washed ashore and was raised by his grandfather Tamanui-ki-te-rangi, who taught him chants and incantations.

cards.prompt: Kuia whose jawbone Māui used as his fish hook
cards.note: Te Ara records that Māui also used her jawbone to beat the sun until it slowed its path across the sky.

cards.label: What is
cards.prompt: Māui's great fish, hauled up from the ocean depths
cards.note: It is the North Island. Ngāti Porou say Hikurangi was the first part to break the surface; Māui baited the hook with his own blood.

cards.label: What is
cards.prompt: The canoe Māui fished from, now an island
cards.note: The South Island, with Rakiura (Stewart Island) as its anchor stone. Ngāti Porou name Māui's canoe Nukutaimemeha, lying upturned on Hikurangi.

cards.label: What is
cards.prompt: What Māui snared with ropes and beat until it slowed
cards.note: Days had been too short for work or sleep. The sun's rays are said to be the remnants of the ropes they used.

cards.label: What is
cards.prompt: What Māui tricked his kuia Mahuika into giving him
cards.note: Te Ara records he took fire from her fingernails and lodged it in trees such as kaikōmako, rimu and tōtara, used for fire making.

cards.label: What is
cards.prompt: What Māui sought by passing through the sleeping Hine-nui-te-pō
cards.note: He warned his companions not to laugh, but laughter woke the goddess and she crushed him; so death remains for all people.

cards.label: Which bird
cards.prompt: Its laughter, in many tellings, woke Hine-nui-te-pō and doomed Māui
cards.note: Te Ara notes some versions blame the moho pererū, the banded rail. Because of this story, a fantail indoors can signal death.

cards.label: Which bird
cards.prompt: Bird Māui became to follow his mother, her skirt colouring its feathers
cards.note: In this tradition the bird was once white; Māui hid Taranga's skirt to delay her, then flew after her still holding it.

cards.prompt: Navigator who chased a great octopus across the ocean to these islands
cards.note: Some tribal narratives make him the first Polynesian to find these islands; the octopus of Muturangi was finally killed in Cook Strait, Raukawakawa.

cards.prompt: Kupe's wife, who in many tellings named the land on first sight
cards.note: Te Ara records that she devised the name Aotearoa on seeing the North Island for the first time, a cloud stretched over the land.

cards.label: Māori name meaning
cards.prompt: Long white cloud
cards.note: Ao is cloud or world, tea is white, roa is long. In one tradition Kuramārōtini named the land after a cloud stretching over it.

cards.label: Which waka
cards.prompt: Kupe's voyaging canoe
cards.note: Also called Matahourua. After Kupe returned to Hawaiki it was re-adzed and renamed Ngātokimatawhaorua by its new captain, Nukutawhiti, who sailed to Hokianga.

cards.prompt: Early ancestor to whom many tribes trace descent
cards.note: Some traditions bring him from Hawaiki, others say he was born here. His pā, Kaputerangi, stood above present-day Whakatāne.

cards.label: What is
cards.prompt: Ancestral homeland, where spirits return after death
cards.note: Some see it as a real Pacific island, others as a spiritual realm. Orators farewell the dead to Hawaiki-nui, Hawaiki-roa, Hawaiki-pāmamao.

cards.prompt: Swam to Mokoia Island at night, guided by her lover's flute
cards.note: Her marriage to Tūtānekai of Ngāti Whakaue, against her people's wishes, is credited with keeping peace in the Rotorua district.

cards.prompt: Woman snatched up by the moon after cursing it
cards.note: She stumbled fetching water when the moon hid behind cloud. She, her gourd and the tree she clutched can be seen on the full moon.

cards.prompt: Ancestor who came to the East Coast on the back of a whale
cards.note: Born Kahutiaterangi, he alone survived when Ruatapu drowned the sons of Uenuku at sea; a rock off Whāngārā is said to be his whale.

cards.label: Which waka
cards.prompt: Captained by Tamatekapua; made final landfall at Maketū
cards.note: Tribes trace descent from the crews of more than 40 waka; the old idea of a single seven-canoe Great Fleet is now discredited.

cards.label: Which waka
cards.prompt: Captained by Hoturoa; laid to rest at Kāwhia
cards.note: Its resting place at Te Ahurei in Kāwhia Harbour is marked by two upright stones; a number of tribes trace their origins to it.

cards.label: Which waka
cards.prompt: Captained by Toroa; landed at Whakatāne
cards.note: In many accounts Wairaka saved the drifting canoe, crying 'Me whakatāne au i ahau', naming Whakatāne; others credit Muriwai.

cards.label: What are
cards.prompt: Supernatural water beings, some guardians, some man-eaters
cards.context: Beings of lakes, rivers and sea
cards.note: Their forms vary between iwi: reptiles, sharks, whales, even logs. A Waikato saying runs 'he piko he taniwha', every bend a taniwha.

cards.label: What is a
cards.prompt: Guardian protecting a people or a place
cards.note: People passing the den of a guardian taniwha would say a karakia and leave an offering, often a green twig.

cards.label: What are
cards.prompt: Fair-haired beings of misty forests and hilltops, who lured people with flute music
cards.note: They feared fire, light and cooked food. Te Ara tells how the chief Kahukura learned net making by joining them at night.

cards.label: What are
cards.prompt: Clawed sea dwellers who came ashore only at night
cards.note: In one tradition Tāwhaki avenged his father by keeping them in a house past dawn, then letting in the killing sunlight.

cards.label: Which taniwha
cards.prompt: Giant reptile taniwha, crushed by trees cut almost through
cards.note: In one tradition the scales he shed leaving his cave at Waimārama became tuatara; a dog under a spell lured him into the trap.

cards.label: Which taniwha
cards.prompt: Guardian placed by Kupe in Cook Strait to protect canoes
cards.note: Some Māori believed the dolphin Pelorus Jack, which escorted ships near French Pass around 1900, was this taniwha returned.

cards.label: Which taniwha
cards.prompt: Two taniwha who shaped Wellington Harbour
cards.note: One smashed through to Cook Strait; the other was stranded, and his spirit flew as a bird to mourn on Tangi te keo, Mt Victoria.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: The Pleiades, whose dawn rising marks the new year
cards.note: Its midwinter rising was a time to remember the dead and celebrate the harvest. Since 2022 it has been a public holiday.

cards.label: Which star
cards.prompt: Rigel, whose rising some iwi take as the new year's sign
cards.note: A saying calls it 'Puanga kai rau', Puanga of abundant food; an elder told Elsdon Best that Puanga strives with Matariki for the year.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: Orion's Belt
cards.note: Te Aka describes these stars as part of the stern of a great sky canoe, Te Waka o Tamarēreti, rising in the early morning.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: The Southern Cross
cards.note: It has at least eight Māori names. Wairarapa Māori saw a gap where storm winds escaped; Tainui saw Te Punga, a sky canoe's anchor.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: The Milky Way
cards.note: In a Ngāti Kahungunu tradition it was the basket that carried the stars to the heavens. Te Mangōroa is another name for it.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: Venus as the morning star
cards.note: Venus has other names too: Tāwera at dawn, and Meremere-tū-ahiahi when it stands out in the western sky after sunset.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: The moon
cards.note: Marama also means a lunar month. In the maramataka, the lunar calendar, each night has its own name, generally beginning with Whiro.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: The sun
cards.note: The chief of the heavenly bodies, called Te Rā-tūoi, the lean sun, in winter and Te Rā-kura, the red sun, in summer.

cards.label: Māori name for
cards.prompt: Sirius, the star of winter
cards.note: Takurua is also a word for winter itself, as in the saying 'Takurua hūpē nui', winter, when your nose runs.
